summary: Converted the verbal 'bundle bloat is trending monotonic' watch-pattern into a mechanical check per CLAUDE_ROOT.md non-negotiable #5. New scripts/bundle-budget.mjs reads dist/assets after vite build, gzips each .js/.css file, and asserts each emitted chunk's gzipped size against a per-pattern budget. Every currently-emitted chunk has an explicit named budget with ~20-40% headroom above today's measured size; catch-all at 3KB gz forces any new unrecognized chunk to surface immediately and prompts an explicit named-budget addition. Wired into the build script so the build gate fails on budget violation. Verify-don't-trust applied to the check itself — deliberately tightened the QrShow budget to 5KB (against current 11.62KB), confirmed exit code 1 with file + budget + over-by + three-fix recipe, restored, confirmed exit code 0 with 18 chunks named. One commit (5a933a9) on branch + main.

outcome.notes: Commit 5a933a9 on branch + main. Mid-session caught a shell-cwd-persisted issue (got 'cannot find module' from earlier cd into dist/assets); fixed with explicit cd /home/user/tapit-wallet before re-running. Pattern-driven catch-all narrowed from 6KB to 3KB after first run found 6 chunks hitting the catch-all (each was a tiny hoisted hook/context, all under 1.5KB gz); added explicit named budgets for each so 0 chunks hit the catch-all in the final state.

uncertainty: Vite's chunk-hoisting behavior is non-deterministic across runs in some edge cases — a small import-graph change can move code between named chunks. The catch-all at 3KB gz is the safety net for the next time that happens. The named budgets have 20-40% headroom; significant feature work could push named chunks over their budgets and the right response then is to either code-split or audit-and-bump.
